title: Prefill/Decode failsafe: kernel arbitration and determinism guard
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Add a failsafe layer to multi-stream prefill+decode capture and replay that ensures forward progress and replay correctness when heuristic kernel arbitration yields non-deterministic execution or capture instability. We will detect divergence early, record lightweight capture metadata hooks, and provide a safe fallback to per-step execution or a conservative kernel set while preserving latency SLOs where possible.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Reproduce a previously flaky multi-stream capture divergence in CI harness and show deterministic failure mode. 2) Implement a capture-snapshot hash and replay-compare path that flags divergence in <2ms per stream. 3) When divergence detected, runtime falls back to conservative kernel selection or step-by-step execution for affected stream(s) without breaking unrelated streams. 4) New telemetry events emitted for capture-start, capture-snapshot, replay-diff, fallback-trigger. 5) End-to-end perf regression <5% median latency for production traffic after enabling the guard in runtime-1.22 canary.
test_plan: - Add micro-harness: synthetic multi-stream workload with controlled kernel arbitration jitter. - CI job that runs harness across 3 recent GPUs (A100, H100, RTX) and fails if divergence not detected. - Add integration scenario with canary traffic (10% weight) and monitor replay-diff rate and latency. - Load test to measure fallback cost and ensure per-route SLOs.
notes: Background: We observe rare non-deterministic outcomes when the kernel selector chooses fused attention kernels vs fallback kernels during interleaved prefill in multi-stream mode. The root cause is timing-sensitive kernel launch ordering and implicit assumptions in cudagraph capture that break when occupancy differs.
Design constraint: Cannot disable cudagraph globally; must guard per-stream and only fall back when necessary to avoid cost regression.

Proposed approach: 1) On capture, insert a tiny sentinel op and compute a cheap 64-bit rolling hash over key intermediate tensors (shape-agnostic fingerprint). 2) Persist capture metadata blob (kernel variant list + sentinel hash) in ephemeral memory accessible at replay time. 3) On replay, compute sentinel hash early and compare. On mismatch, trigger fallback path: either (A) replay that stream in step mode (no graph) or (B) re-capture with conservative kernel whitelist. Choice B preferred when capture cost amortizes for long-running cohorts.
Telemetry: Add events: capture.started, capture.completed, capture.snapshot_hash, replay.started, replay.compare_result, replay.fallback.mode, fallback.duration, fallback.reason.
Safety: Ensure sentinel ops are no-op for outcomes; they must not change numerical state. Use a masked XOR-reduction over a small selection of tensors to produce hash.

Performance trade-off: Snapshot/hash adds ~200-500us at capture end; acceptable because captures are infrequent and detection avoids costly silent corruption. Fallback per-step execution increases tokens latency for affected stream by 10-40% depending on model length; we will prioritize re-capture flow for long-running sessions.

Related PR references and artifacts: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1245 (initial harness + sentinel shim), Design doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/confluence/display/RUNTIME/Prefill+Failsafe+Design, Perf dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/runtime/cuda-graph-failsafe-canary

2026-03-02 - Design review (A. Patel): Approved sentinel approach but requested adding a conservative kernel whitelist option to avoid per-step slowdown for heavy cohorts. Action: add re-capture-with-whitelist flow.

2026-03-10 - Liam Oconnor: Buffer lifetime fix pushed in https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1258. Added unit test for ephemeral metadata eviction under preemption.

2026-03-12 - Maya Chen: Canary started on runtime-1.22 with 5% traffic on eu-west; first 48h: replay-diff rate 0.003% and 17 triggered fallbacks. Investigating two fallbacks that escalated to step-mode; both correlated with model length > 2048 and rapid small-batch bursts.

2026-03-13 - Next steps (Liam): 1) Implement re-capture-with-whitelist decision heuristic (cost model added). 2) Add CI matrix job with H100 and A100 and deterministic seed across streams. 3) Postmortem template for any customer-visible divergence event. owner_notes: Focus next on decision heuristic: use expected session length + token remaining + recapture cost to choose between step-mode vs whitelist recapture. Instrument recapture latency so scheduler can decide automatically in future.
